features.detail: Create, search, join and leave rooms modelled on sceNpMatching2. A search sees only the rooms of its own title, with each room's external data. Room messages, owner kicks, owner handoff when the owner leaves, and member pushes with each peer's address and P2P port.
features.note: Upstream work. `KICK_MEMBER` removes a member but does not prevent rejoining.

features.detail: External and internal room data (only the owner writes it), room flags that searchers see (`SET_ROOM_DATA` which 2), and member data sent with `CREATE_ROOM` and `JOIN_ROOM` and returned in every member entry.
features.note: External and internal data are upstream work (0.1.0). Room flags and member data are newer, so clients built against 0.1.0 no longer match.

features.detail: An 8-character code per room (`SET_ROOM_ACCESS`, `JOIN_BY_CODE`, `GET_ROOM_ACCESS`). The room leaves search and the status page, which counts unlisted rooms. A connection that sends too many wrong codes is closed.
features.note: Protocol 0.4: `HELLO_ACK` flags bit 1 says the server has them. Codes are never logged.

features.detail: Matching2 room passwords, private slots and join by room ID. A relay-only variant that keeps members' addresses hidden from each other is also wanted.
features.note: The relay-only variant is not designed yet.

features.detail: Modelled on sceNpScore: each player's best score is kept, a tie goes to whoever scored first, boards are higher-is-better or lower-is-better, and ranks are read by range or by online ID.
features.note: Upstream work. Kept in memory: a restart empties every board. Opt-in storage is planned (store-sqlite).

features.detail: Names are compared case-insensitively. A HELLO with a name held from another address gets ERROR 8 (name taken); from the same address it is the same player reconnecting, and the old connection is closed.
features.note: No passwords: a name is not authenticated.

features.detail: sceNpBasic: a friends list (everyone on the same server), presence (online, title, room), invites and join-a-friend, player history and a block list.
features.note: Not in the server today.

features.detail: Optional accounts next to the default of a name per player: a credential per server kept on the player's machine, sign-in through a generic OpenID Connect provider, or with Discord or GitHub.
features.note: Not started. Needs the opt-in database (store-sqlite) first, and the scope in ROADMAP.md says no accounts or passwords, so that needs changing too. The default would stay a name per player.

features.detail: `-max-rooms`, `-max-player-rooms`, `-max-conns-per-addr`, `-max-req-rate` (requests per second per connection) and a size cap on room data. A request over a limit is refused; a connection over the rate is closed. Each refusal is logged at warn level.
features.evidence: server/limits_test.go, TestBlobLimit, TestPlayerRoomLimit, TestConnLimitPerAddr, TestRequestRateLimit, TestLogHelloAndRefusals
features.note: These limits cover TCP. Main also has bounded UDP admission and drop counters; see the partial net-guardrails row.

features.detail: `-log-level` (debug, info, warn, error), `-v` as debug, `-log-format` text or json, and `-log-file` to append to a file (mode 0600). Connection and room refusals are logged at warn level; UDP drops use aggregate counters, with one warning per player for a mismatched probe. Tokens, room codes, peer keys and query strings are never logged, at any level (`TestLogsHoldNoSecrets` drives a session at debug level in both formats).
features.evidence: server/logging.go, TestLogHelloAndRefusals, TestLogLevelAndFormat, TestLogStatusRefusalKeepsTokenOut, #4, TestLogsHoldNoSecrets, server/log_secrets_test.go
features.note: Not checked: no test covers `-log-file`. The server does not rotate the file.

features.feature: Status page and /api/stats, with a token
features.detail: A read-only page and JSON on a separate listener, off unless `-http` names an address (`127.0.0.1:36101` keeps it on localhost). `-http-token` requires a token (`Authorization: Bearer`, or `?token=`), and the server warns at start when the page is reachable from elsewhere without one. Since v0.4.0 the page uses the project palette (dark, with the gruvbox-material light mode), Rooms/Leaderboards tabs, System/Light/Dark and browser-local text size, spacing and contrast-checked custom colours.
features.evidence: server/api.go, TestStatusToken, TestReachable, TestStatusPageOff, TestStatusPageOn, docs/status.png, server/status_theme_test.go, TestStatusTerminalPage, TestStatusThemeAuthenticationAndHeaders, tools/status_browser_check.mjs, docs/running.md
features.note: The page and /api/stats are upstream work (0.1.0); the token is the fork's.

features.detail: `/metrics` in the Prometheus text format, off by default, with the status page's token rules: connections, rooms, refusals, UDP probes and relay traffic. No names, addresses, room codes or tokens in any label.
features.note: Not started. Needs the counters from net-guardrails first.

features.detail: Example Prometheus scrape config, alert rules and a Grafana dashboard in `deploy/`, written from the real metric names.
features.note: After metrics-endpoint.

features.detail: `-trusted-proxies` (CIDRs or addresses) and `-proxy-protocol` (a PROXY v1 or v2 header required on the game TCP port from a listed proxy), and forwarded headers for the status page log. The real client address then counts for the limits, the name rule, `public_ip` and the log.
features.evidence: server/proxy.go, TestReadProxyHeader, TestClientAddr, TestProxyHeaderFromUntrustedPeerIsJunk, TestTrustedPeerWithoutHeaderIsClosed, TestLimitUsesRealAddress, #9, #12
features.note: Off by default. UDP is not proxied. See docs/running.md.

features.feature: Settings file, service unit and Traefik example
features.detail: `deploy/` holds `re-psn.env.example` (every setting, commented), a systemd unit and a Traefik config that sends PROXY v2. The release archives carry them as `examples/`.
features.note: `scripts/check-deploy.sh` checks the env file and the unit against the server's flags. The Traefik run (Traefik 3.1 under Podman) is recorded in docs/running.md; no run of the systemd unit is recorded.

features.detail: An nginx `stream` block with `proxy_protocol on;` (PROXY v1) and an HAProxy config with `send-proxy-v2`.
features.note: Not checked: neither config has been run against the server (docs/running.md says so).

features.detail: A stock Caddy 2 HTTP reverse-proxy example in `deploy/caddy/`, copied into future release archives with the other deployment examples. Defaults to loopback and leaves game TCP/UDP direct.
features.note: Written from the official Caddy documentation; not run or validated with Caddy. No layer-4 plugin is included. The existing HTTP token check is preserved and client-supplied CF-Connecting-IP is removed before forwarding.

features.detail: A disabled systemd-journal filter/jail example for repeated HTTP status-token refusals. Uses JSON logs and a host TCP status-port action, with setup, firewall placement, validation and recovery instructions.
features.note: Offline synthetic HTTP/logger and native fail2ban-engine checks do not establish live journal/firewall enforcement. Game TCP/UDP, proxy/CDN and bridged-container enforcement are outside the sample's scope; install and verify fail2ban separately.

features.detail: A two-stage Dockerfile and a compose file in `docker/`, configured only by `RE_PSN_*` variables. The status page is off until `RE_PSN_HTTP` is set.
features.evidence: docker/Dockerfile, docker/docker-compose.yml, docker/docker-compose.host.yml, docker/docker-compose.test.yml, docker/README.md, lab/run.sh, #11
features.note: A Podman 6.1 run is recorded in docker/README.md, and the NAT lab builds the image with Docker in CI. The v0.2.0 image is pushed to ghcr.io (amd64 and arm64, unsigned; arm64 not run). The server runs as a non-root user and the bases are pinned by digest. Opt-in host-networking compose files, one hardened for a shared test host, are for Linux only. Compose under Podman is not tested.

features.detail: Every flag can be set as `RE_PSN_<FLAG>`; the old `PSNR_<FLAG>` names still work as aliases. A flag wins, then `RE_PSN_`, then `PSNR_`. An old name logs a warning that names the variables, never the value. `-tcp-addr` and `-udp-addr` give the two game sockets their own addresses. A bad value stops the server at start.
features.evidence: server/config.go, TestEnvAlias, TestEnvNoticeHidesValue, TestFlagBeatsEnv, TestEnvBad, TestListenAddrs, #8, #17
features.note: No config file yet.

features.detail: A storage layer with an in-memory backend, the leaderboards wired through it, and a `-db` (`RE_PSN_DB`) setting. Off by default, so nothing changes unless a host turns it on.
features.evidence: server/store/store.go, server/store/storetest/storetest.go, TestMemoryContract, TestDBSetting, TestDBNotLogged, TestScoreStoreFailure, TestScoresOutsideRoomLock, #22
features.note: Only `off` and `memory` exist, so scores are still kept in memory and lost on restart; other schemes stop the start. First step of opt-in storage (store-sqlite is next).

features.detail: An SQLite backend with a pure-Go driver, so the release archives stay static, and migrations built into the binary. With it on, scores survive a restart. The connection string is never logged.
features.note: Not started. The server's first third-party Go module. Player names and bans would follow with accounts.

features.detail: Documented backup and restore for each database: a backup command or a copy procedure for SQLite; a dump command with timer and cron examples for PostgreSQL and MariaDB. How long backups are kept is up to the host.
features.note: Not started. Comes with store-sqlite.

features.detail: A PostgreSQL backend for hosts who bring their own database; the server does not run or manage it.
features.note: After store-sqlite.

features.detail: A MariaDB backend for hosts who bring their own database; the server does not run or manage it.
features.note: After store-sqlite.

features.detail: A data-free `/healthz` endpoint on the opt-in status listener, guarded by the existing HTTP token, and bounded shutdown that closes listeners and accepted client/relay sockets. A guide covers probe results, supervisors and what players lose on restart.
features.note: Health is 200 only while both game serving loops are active, 503 during startup/shutdown or after a loop exits. Loopback and subprocess tests cover shutdown; systemd/container restarts and remote failover are not run. Rooms and scores remain in memory and are lost on restart. No database retry is needed until a network backend exists.

features.detail: Docs and example files for a standby server: a floating address (keepalived) or a proxy's health checks, both servers on the same database, one active at a time. No election or replication inside the server.
features.note: Not started. After ha-restart; the shared database needs store-postgres or store-mariadb. Live rooms are lost on failover.

features.detail: Several servers behind one address, each room wholly on one server, with a routing layer that sends a new room or a join to the right one.
features.note: On the back burner: revisited after ha-restart and ha-failover exist and one server is not enough.

features.detail: Rooms that survive the loss of a server.
features.note: Needs replicated live state; out of scope for a server of this size.

features.detail: A player's P2P socket sends the server a UDP PROBE. The server records the public endpoint and gives each viewer the address that works from where they are: the public one from another network, the LAN address from the same one.
features.note: Upstream work. The NAT lab runs it in Docker in CI.

features.detail: `-relay`, off by default: streams into a player behind a router go through the server, and datagrams go through the server's UDP port when punching does not get through (as with a symmetric NAT).
features.note: Upstream work. Uses the server's bandwidth; there is no per-player budget yet (net-guardrails).

features.detail: PROBE and RELAY packets are accepted only from the IP address of the player's TCP connection. A probe's `local_ip` is kept only if it is private, carrier-grade NAT, link-local or the probe's own source. `-udp-any-source` turns the check off.
features.note: A Podman run is recorded in docker/README.md.

features.detail: Bounded per-source-IP UDP packet admission shared by probes, relay and invalid traffic, plus aggregate drop-reason counters in /api/stats. The token bucket tracks at most 4096 sources, expires idle entries and rejects new sources at capacity.
features.evidence: server/udp_guard.go, server/udp.go, server/relay.go, TestUDPLimiter, TestUDPAdmissionRealPackets, TestUDPCountersStatsAuthenticationAndConcurrency, docs/udp-guardrails.md
features.note: Initial packet limiter only: default 1000 packets/second with the same burst, configurable with -max-udp-rate and 0 for off; players behind one NAT share it. Per-player relay byte/datagram budgets, payload and TCP stream limits, failed-token blocking and UDP fuzz coverage remain planned. A larger token needs a protocol version bump.

features.detail: A check for players and hosts that says where a connection fails (server reachable, HELLO accepted, UDP probe answered, NAT behaviour, peer reachable, relay available) and shows round trip, loss and whether each peer is up.
features.note: Not designed yet.

features.detail: Open a player's P2P port on their router automatically.
features.note: Not started.

features.detail: An opt-in, disabled-by-default Medius-compatible frontend for a named title/build profile, starting with synthetic local transport and discovery. Unknown or unsupported profiles, versions, application IDs and messages fail explicitly.
features.note: Not implemented. Candidate Killzone 3 BCUS98234 update 1.14, app ID 23044: compatibility not tested; not supported.

features.detail: Logical sessions across service sockets and profile-specific lobby operations, with only an explicitly unauthenticated synthetic local TicketLogin envelope.
features.note: Not implemented; no PSN authentication or real tickets.

features.detail: A data path considered only after the selected profile's transport, membership and authorization requirements are evidenced.
features.note: Not implemented. The data plane, NAT and DME requirements are unknown; no psnr reuse is promised.

features.detail: Consider additional explicitly selected title/build profiles, each with its own evidence and failure rules.
features.note: Not started; no general Medius or multi-title compatibility is claimed.

features.detail: One file with no dependencies and no threads: `psnr_send` returns a request id, and `psnr_poll` hands out replies and pushes; sends and automatic heartbeat writes can wait for socket writability. It also builds the UDP probe and relay packets.
features.note: Upstream work. The integration guide documents ownership and timeout limits. `TestCClient` also compiles/runs the minimal example; it skips without a C compiler, and Linux CI requires execution.

features.detail: `app/internal/client`: a Go client for the TCP protocol, for the desktop app. HELLO, heartbeat, create, search, join and leave rooms, record and read scores, and the member and route pushes, with typed messages and errors. `re-psn-app check HOST:PORT` uses it.
features.note: Room data and messages, kicks, invite-only rooms, relay streams and UDP are not in it yet.

features.detail: `re-psn-app` with no arguments: a first-run choice of Play, Host or Both with the online ID and the server, a menu and content pane (one at a time under 70 columns), a Status screen with Rooms and Leaderboards tabs over the game protocol or an explicitly configured HTTP status source, a Settings screen that saves `re-psn.ini`, and a dark or light theme in the website colours. Built on Bubble Tea and Lip Gloss.
features.evidence: app/internal/tui, TestFirstRunChooser, TestStatusTabs, TestConnectionErrorsAreText, TestNarrowLayout, TestThemeToggle, TestSettings, app/internal/desktop, TestLaunchSyntheticTerminalProcess, app/internal/tui/http_status.go, TestHTTPStatusNativeViewsAndQuery, TestHTTPStatusFallbackUsesProtocol
features.note: Partial: no Host screen, room joining, launch profiles or theme presets yet. Linux desktop starts without a TTY can open a supported terminal; Windows uses its console. Synthetic startup tests ran; physical desktops/emulators remain unverified. The optional HTTP source adds uptime, connection counts, public-room members/age and board leader summaries with bounded authenticated fetches and game-protocol fallback. The game protocol still lacks those extra fields; neither source reports server version. Driven in tmux on Linux; not tried on Windows or macOS terminals.

features.detail: A terminal program for players and hosts: launch profiles per game, a host mode, and a check of the connection.
features.note: Not started. One executable per platform, with nothing else to install.

features.detail: A local web UI served by the same program, and a graphical app on Windows, with the same screens as the terminal UI.
features.note: Not started. After client-desktop.

features.detail: Find on LAN in the desktop app (`f` in Settings, Ctrl+F while typing the server): the Go client broadcasts one 64-byte UDP request from a temporary socket, collects the 52-byte replies for about 1.5 s, drops anything with the wrong length, type or nonce, and lists name, address:port, players, relay and version; the chosen address fills the server field. Typing host:port still works.
features.evidence: app/internal/client/discover.go, TestDiscoverValidReply, TestDiscoverIgnoresBadDatagrams, TestDiscoverDeduplicates, TestDiscoverTimeoutIsEmptyNotError, TestDiscoverSanitisesText, TestDiscoverCancel, app/internal/tui/lan_test.go, TestFindOnLANShowsListAndFillsServer, TestFindOnLANNoneFound, TestFindOnLANWhileTypingTheServer, TestFindOnLANFirstRun
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. Finds only servers started with -discover. Tested against a fake responder and, by hand, against a real server on loopback; not a real broadcast across a network. IPv4 and the local subnet only. `server = auto` in re-psn.ini is not supported.

features.detail: Colour presets in the desktop apps: the project palette by default, then gruvbox, catppuccin, kanagawa and melange. A preset is a data file shared by the apps and the README art.
features.note: Not started. A preset ships only after its project's licence is read and credited in NOTICE.md. The terminal UI falls back to the terminal's own 16 colours and respects NO_COLOR.

features.detail: Dark, Light or System (the default): presets carry a dark and a light variant where their project has both, and System follows the OS or the terminal background and switches while the app runs.
features.note: Desktop presets and system-following remain planned. The server status page supports browser System/Light/Dark and local appearance controls; see status-page.

features.detail: Edit named colour slots (background, surface, text, muted, accent, good, warn, bad) as hex values, with a contrast warning below 4.5:1, import and export, saved per user and per mode.
features.note: Not started. A bad value falls back to the default preset.

features.detail: Go fuzz targets for the frame parser, the request handlers and the PROXY header parser. Their seed inputs run with every `go test`.
features.note: CI runs the seeds only; longer fuzzing runs are by hand. The UDP packets have no fuzz target yet.

features.detail: gofmt, go vet, `go test -race` on Linux (with the C client) and `go test` on Windows, govulncheck, gitleaks over the full history, the NAT lab in Docker, and CodeQL for Go and the workflows. Actions are pinned and permissions are read-only by default.
features.note: Dependabot proposes version updates. A focused local loopback runner requires native C-client and Go app-client conformance checks to execute; synthetic loopback only.

features.detail: `scripts/release-build.sh` builds static binaries for windows/amd64, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 into `re-psn-vX.Y.Z-<os>-<arch>` archives and one SHA256SUMS listing them. A pushed version tag makes a draft pre-release; a second workflow checks a published one.

features.detail: `scripts/build-appimage.sh` packs the linux/amd64 server binary and its examples as `re-psn-vX.Y.Z-x86_64.AppImage`, with appimagetool 1.9.1 and the type-2 runtime 20251108, both downloaded by the release workflow and checked against pinned SHA-256 hashes. A smoke test compares its `-h` and version with the binary's, and it is listed in SHA256SUMS.
features.note: Published in the v0.2.0 pre-release (2026-11-06); the release workflow built it on a runner and passed its smoke test. It was also built and run on one x86_64 Linux machine, with FUSE and with `--appimage-extract-and-run`. x86_64 only, unsigned.

features.detail: `scripts/install.sh` (Linux amd64 and arm64, POSIX sh) and `scripts/install.ps1` (Windows amd64; written for PowerShell 5.1 and 7, tested on 7 only) install the server for the current user from a GitHub release, newest or pinned, after checking the download against SHA256SUMS. No sudo or administrator rights, no profile edits; `--dry-run`, `--dir`, `--appimage`, `-AddToPath`.
features.evidence: scripts/install.sh, scripts/install.ps1, scripts/test-install.sh, scripts/test-install.ps1, TestCheckReleaseAssets, docs/installing.md

The Linux tests run under dash, bash and BusyBox ash with a fake release, and the published v0.4.0 `install.sh` installed that release on Linux amd64 into a temporary directory; `install.ps1` has not installed from a published release. The PowerShell fake-release tests have passed under PowerShell 7 on Linux and Windows CI; PowerShell 5.1 remains untested. No macOS builds, so no macOS support.

features.detail: Written steps for cutting a release (tag, notes from CHANGELOG.md, checking the draft, publishing), a check that the version in the code and in CHANGELOG.md agree, and a dry run of the release workflow before the first tag.
features.note: VERSION, the version check (TestVersionAgrees), scripts/bump-version.sh and scripts/release-notes.sh are built and docs/releasing.md has the steps; the release workflow builds its notes with the notes script and checks that a tag is v + VERSION, and the first tag, v0.2.0 (2026-11-06), ran the whole path: the dry run, the tag step and the draft job passed, and the draft was published by hand after its assets were read back. No fixed release day: while things are worked out, pre-releases (v0.x, marked pre-release) come whenever there is something worth trying.

features.detail: Sign `re-psn.exe` so Windows does not warn about an unsigned program, and sign the checksums.
features.note: The exe and SHA256SUMS are unsigned today.

features.detail: `docs/features.tsv` holds one row per feature with its status and evidence, and `tools/features.py` generates this page. CI fails when the page is stale, a row is malformed, or evidence is missing.
The architecture, reverse proxy, relay and NAT lab diagrams are Mermaid, which GitHub renders.
features.note: No generated images to keep in step.

features.detail: Every doc in Markdown with one layout, including the deploy and Docker READMEs with diagrams.
features.note: The offline repo-check guard validates tracked local Markdown links and anchors in CI.

features.detail: A page on how players reach a server: same LAN, port forwarding, a public server with `-relay`, a VPN overlay (Tailscale, ZeroTier) or a reverse proxy, with what each needs, its limits, diagrams and links to the overlays' official documentation.
features.note: Not tested: re-psn has not been run over Tailscale, ZeroTier or any other overlay. Overlay addressing was imitated with network namespaces only.

features.detail: A README that says what re-psn is, with a quick start, the available features linking to this page, installation, configuration and credit to upstream.
features.note: Example output comes from real local runs; the settings table was checked against the server flags. The banner comes from the art generator (docs-art).

Terminal images are drawn only from transcripts of real runs (`docs/art/transcripts/`, recorded by `tools/art/capture.sh`). CI renders again and fails when a byte differs.

features.note: The README shows the banner; the social image is uploaded by hand in the repository settings; its example stays text, and the terminal images are kept for the site. Images are dark only; the light colours are in the palette for later. Fonts are not committed.

features.detail: A static page built from the features list, the version, the settings table and the changelog by `tools/site.py`: overview, features with status tags, roadmap, settings, install, connect, docs and credits. With `site/terminal.js` (no dependencies) the page becomes a terminal-style interface: menu, content and a command line with the commands `features`, `roadmap`, `settings`, `install`, `connect`, `changelog`, `docs` and more, suggestions while typing (a dimmed completion and a list of up to eight matches, taken with Tab, Right arrow, Enter or a tap), Tab completion, history, a dark and a light theme chosen with a System / Light / Dark switch in the header or the `theme` command (the same choice, remembered in the browser), colour from the full gruvbox-material palette with every text colour checked at 4.5:1 or more, and scrolling tabs and tappable chips on a phone (a phone starts in the plain view); the same page works without script, and a plain view link switches the interface off. No third-party loads, a content security policy that allows only this site, and the colours of the README art. `pages.yml` deploys `site/` to GitHub Pages. Command output has a file header, line-number gutter, frame and syntax-style colours.

Unit tests and optional headless-browser checks cover command typing, autocomplete/history, selection without gutter numbers, dark/light and system-theme changes, narrow layouts and static fallbacks. A real keyboard, screen reader and physical phone have not been tried. The font remains the visitor's monospace; self-hosting is not added.

features.detail: An offline CI check of tracked root filenames and top-level directories, local Markdown links and heading/explicit anchors, and static repository input paths in workflows and Dependabot.
features.note: Python standard library and Git only. Does not fetch external links, evaluate arbitrary shell/YAML expressions or validate generated artifact paths.

features.detail: A source-pinned guide for ps3recomp ports and direct C/C++ adapters: build/startup, callback ownership, message lifetime, failure handling and peer/relay boundaries. A synthetic minimal C example exercises HELLO and room search in the required native-client test.
features.note: Runtime integration was inspected at the linked upstream revision; no actual title was built or run for the guide. Native example/conformance checks are synthetic loopback evidence, not gameplay or NAT certification.

features.detail: `/api/stats` and the status page label rooms and leaderboards with the game's name and serials, for example `[Killzone 3 (BCUS98234, BCES01007)]`, from a small table embedded in the server (four games so far); a game the table does not know keeps its communication ID. The protocol is unchanged.
features.evidence: server/titles.go, server/titles.tsv, TestTitleTableRows, TestParseGamesSkipsBadLines, TestTitleLabel, TestStatusShowsGameLabelsSorted
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. The table is never fetched at run time.

features.detail: Each public room has `verified` (members whose UDP probe the server accepted on this connection) and the top level has `verified_players`; the page shows '(N verified)' beside a room's member count. The protocol is unchanged.
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. A count of probes the server accepted, not a check of who the players are.

features.detail: `/api/stats` reports the version, whether the relay is on, the payload the relay has carried, the limits in force and the TCP connections refused (per address, request rate). Aggregate only; no address or player. The protocol is unchanged.
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. Counts are since start. `relay_bytes` is payload, not interface traffic.

features.detail: HEARTBEAT may carry the player's own last round trip (`rtt_ms`, 2 bytes); the server shows it next to each member as reported by the player. The C client and the app's Go client send it once a title opts in (recommended, off by default).
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. Reported by the player and not verified; display only. The round trip includes the server's own time.

features.detail: `-relay-force` (`RE_PSN_RELAY_FORCE`, off by default, needs `-relay`) sends every stream through the relay, even between players who could connect directly, so the relay can be tested from one network. Datagrams are not forced.
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. For testing only: it uses the host's bandwidth.

features.detail: `-no-peer-titles` lists communication IDs of titles that use no peer traffic: their players get no UDP probe reply, no relay for datagrams or streams, no relay route and no relay flag in HELLO_ACK, and still use rooms and scores. Other titles on the server are unaffected.
features.evidence: server/title_peer.go, TestNoPeerTitleProbe, TestNoPeerTitleHelloFlag, TestNoPeerTitleRoute, TestNoPeerTitleRelayRefused, TestNoPeerTitlesFlagAndEnv
features.note: Not in v0.5.0. A list of IDs, not a per-title profile file. Hole punching itself is client-side: it stops because the server never learns the endpoint. Tested on loopback with a client written for the tests, not with a real title.

features.detail: `GET_CAPS` (0x04) after HELLO returns `CAPS` (0x94): a bit set of what this server offers this player (rooms, scores, room codes, peer keys, the UDP probe, the relay, LAN discovery) and the server version. The probe and relay bits are per title, so a title in `-no-peer-titles` sees them clear. The C client has the constants and `psnr_caps_parse`.
features.evidence: server/caps.go, TestCapsDefault, TestCapsRelayDiscoverAndNoPeer, TestCapsNeedsHello, client/psnr.c, client/test_psnr.c
features.note: Not in v0.5.0. A server before this answers the request with ERROR 1. Tested on loopback with a test client and the C client; no real title asks for it yet.

features.detail: A client may ask with `PEER_AUTH`; each pair of members who both asked then gets one new random 16-byte key in a `PEER_KEY` push, for tagging their direct packets. Opt-in; clients that do not ask are unaffected.
features.evidence: server/peerkey.go, TestPeerKeyPair, TestPeerKeysPerPair, TestPeerKeyNeedsBoth, TestPeerKeyLateOptIn, TestPeerKeyRepeatAndRejoin, TestPeerAuthNeedsHello
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. No client uses the keys yet, and nothing is tagged on the wire. The keys travel over plain TCP, so this gives no confidentiality and no protection from someone who can read a player's network traffic.

features.detail: `-lan-public-addr IP` (`RE_PSN_LAN_PUBLIC_ADDR`, IPv4, off by default) gives players on public addresses the host's address and the member's P2P port for a player who connected from a private, CGNAT or link-local address. The host forwards each such P2P port. Players on private addresses are unaffected.
features.evidence: server/udp.go, TestLANPublicAddrOff, TestLANPublicAddrRemoteViewer, TestLANPublicAddrLANViewer, TestLANPublicAddrPublicMember, TestLANPublicAddrParse, TestLANPublicAddrBadFlag, TestLANPublicAddrFlagAndEnv
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. Off by default. Several LAN players behind one forward need distinct P2P ports; the relay covers a failed connection.

features.detail: `-discover` (`RE_PSN_DISCOVER`, off by default) answers a 64-byte DISCOVER sent to the game UDP port with a 52-byte reply: TCP and UDP ports, relay flag, player count, name (`-name`) and version. Only private, carrier-grade NAT, link-local and loopback senders are answered, under the UDP rate limit.
features.evidence: server/discover.go, TestDiscoverReply, TestDiscoverOffNoReply, TestDiscoverWrongLengthAndOtherTypes, TestDiscoverSourceClasses, TestDiscoverPublicSourceRefused, TestDiscoverRateLimited, TestDiscoverNameRules
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. Off by default. Server side only: no client helper yet. A broadcast does not cross subnets or Wi-Fi client isolation.

features.feature: LAN discovery in the C client
features.detail: `psnr_discover` broadcasts one UDP request from its own temporary socket and returns the LAN servers that answer, with their ports, relay flag, player count, name and version.
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. Finds only servers started with -discover. Tested against a fake responder and, by hand, against a real server on loopback; not a real broadcast across a network. Does not cross subnets or client-isolated Wi-Fi. The Windows build broadcasts to 255.255.255.255 only; CI compiles the client with MSVC but does not run it on Windows.

features.feature: Host connect policy in the C client
features.detail: `psnr_set_connect_policy` registers one callback that the client asks before it opens a TCP connection: the connection `psnr_connect` and `psnr_connect_timeout` make (once per resolved address, with the host as typed) and each relay leg (`psnr_stream_connect`, `psnr_stream_accept`). A refusal skips that address, or returns -1 for a relay leg; refusing every address gives NULL and `psnr_connect_error()` is `PSNR_E_POLICY`. No callback means today's behaviour.
features.note: Not in v0.5.0. Process-wide, set before the first connect; not covered: `psnr_discover` and the title's own P2P socket. IPv4 only, like the client. Tested against a real server on loopback; each check fails with its hook removed.

features.detail: With a status URL set, the Status screen has a read-only Server tab (Tab cycles Rooms, Leaderboards, Server): version, uptime, relay on or off, the limits in force (0 shown as none), TCP refusals and UDP drop counters, and the payload carried by the relay with a bytes-per-second rate computed between two refreshes. A counter that goes down is shown as server restarted and the rate baseline starts again. Fields an older server omits are shown as not reported by this server, never as 0 or off. Nothing is changed on the server and the token is never shown.
features.evidence: app/internal/tui/server_stats.go, app/internal/tui/server_view.go, app/internal/tui/server_view_test.go, TestDecodeServerStatsAllFields, TestDecodeServerStatsOldServer, TestDecodeServerStatsPartial, TestServerTrackRate, TestServerTrackCounterWentDown, TestServerViewNewServer, TestServerViewOldServer, TestServerViewRestart, TestServerViewNoToken, TestServerTabOnlyWithStatusURL
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. Needs a server that reports the fields (newer than v0.4.0); older servers show not reported. Relay bytes and the rate are payload carried by the relay, not network bandwidth. Checked by hand against a real server on loopback.

features.detail: An opt-in listener of its own (`-admin`, `-admin-read-token-file`, TLS for a non-loopback address) with one route, `GET /admin/v1/state`, for a read token: version, uptime, relay, limits, TCP and UDP refusal counts and the ban count (always 0 for now), no address or player. Failed requests get a growing capped delay and one fail2ban-shaped log line; the token file is read again on SIGHUP.
features.note: Experimental and not in a release. Read-only: no action, no ban, no limit change, and no app view yet; those are separate changes. Not run against a reverse proxy, on Windows, or on a container secret mount.

features.detail: The release build makes `re-psn-app-vX.Y.Z-linux-amd64.tar.gz`, `-linux-arm64.tar.gz` and `-windows-amd64.zip` from `app/` (static, no cgo, version set from the tag), each with `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md` and the app README, listed in `SHA256SUMS`. A release has ten assets.
features.note: Not in v0.4.0. `install.sh --app` and `install.ps1 -App` install it (tested against a fake release only). The release workflow has not built them on a tag; the Windows and arm64 binaries are cross-built and not run.

paragraphs: re-psn answers the matchmaking and leaderboard calls of a statically recompiled PS3 game, for a group running its own server: a LAN, a VPN, or friends connecting to one person's machine. The server keeps rooms and leaderboards and tells each player where the others are. Game traffic goes directly between players, and through the server only when two players cannot reach each other and the host has turned the relay on.
It is a fork of [psnr](https://github.com/sp00nznet/psnr) by sp00nz: a Go server and a one-file C client, with no accounts and no public instance.
about.notice: Unofficial; not affiliated with Sony. No game files, keys or firmware are in the repository or needed from it. Play only games you own.

install.archives: Archives for Linux (amd64, arm64) and Windows (amd64), and a Linux x86_64 AppImage, all unsigned, with a `SHA256SUMS` file. Check a download on Linux:
install.verify_windows: On Windows, compare the output of `Get-FileHash <archive>` with the line in `SHA256SUMS`.
install.container_note: Podman works the same way. See [docker/README.md](docker/README.md).
install.source_note: You need Go 1.22 or newer; a C compiler only for the C client and its tests.

connect.intro: Players on one LAN or VPN need nothing forwarded. Otherwise the host forwards a port, runs a public server, or uses an overlay network such as Tailscale or ZeroTier; the relay is the fallback when two players cannot reach each other.
points: Game connection and address probes: `:36100`, TCP and UDP, open to every player.
Status page: `none (off)`, for the host only; it lists every online ID.
Each player's P2P port (UDP and TCP) must be reachable by the other players; the game opens it.
connect.client: A game reaches the server through the C client in `client/psnr.c`, via ps3recomp's NP modules. That side is upstream's work; [docs/connecting.md](docs/connecting.md) covers each way to connect.

scenarios.title: Direct: players on one LAN or VPN
scenarios.summary: Both players can reach each other, so the server only introduces them. Game traffic never touches it.

steps.caption: Player A says who it is and which UDP port its game listens on.
The server answers with a user id, the address it sees, a token and a flags byte.
Player A opens a room.
The room exists, and A is its first member.
Player B connects the same way.
The server answers B.
B asks for rooms of its title that are not full.
A's room is in the list.
B joins it.
The reply carries every member's address and game port, so B knows where A is.
B sends game datagrams straight to A. The server is not on the path.

scenarios.title: Hole punch: two ordinary home routers
scenarios.summary: Each player is behind a router. The server learns each router's public address from a probe, the players punch through, and then talk directly.

steps.caption: Player A connects and gives its game port.
The answer includes the token that A's probes will carry.
A opens a room.
A is its first member.
From its game socket, A sends a UDP probe, so the server sees A's router's public address and port.
The server tells A what it saw.
Player B connects.
The server answers B.
B probes from its game socket too.
The server tells B what it saw.
B joins A's room.
The member entry for A carries the router address and port from A's probe.
Both players send PUNCH packets to each other's router address, which opens each router for the other.
Game datagrams now go directly between the players.

scenarios.title: Relayed: one player behind a symmetric NAT
scenarios.summary: B's router picks a new port for every destination, so the punch cannot work. A server run with -relay carries the game traffic instead. The room steps are as in the scenarios above and are left out here; the server sends ROUTE to both players, and only A's copy is shown.

steps.caption: Player A connects.
The flags byte says the server relays.
Player B connects.
The server answers B.
A probes; its router keeps one port, so the server sees a usable address.
B probes; its router maps a new port for each destination.
A punches towards the address the server saw for B. It does not reach B.
The server tells A that streams to B go through the relay.
A opens a new TCP connection to the server and asks for a stream to B.
The server offers B the stream, on B's control connection.
B opens its own new TCP connection to the server and accepts, within 10 seconds.
The stream is ready on A's side.
And on B's side.
From here the server copies the stream's bytes between the two connections. UDP game datagrams go through the relay as well.

scenarios.title: Blocked: the relay is off
scenarios.summary: The same failed punch as above, but the server was not started with -relay, so it carries nothing. The room steps are as in the scenarios above and are left out here.

steps.caption: Player A connects.
The flags byte says the server does not relay.
Player B connects.
The server answers B.
A probes.
B probes; its router maps a new port for each destination.
The punch towards B's seen address does not reach B.
There is no ROUTE and no stream: the server has nothing to offer. The players need a port forward, or a shared VPN such as Tailscale.

credits: sp00nz ([sp00nznet](https://github.com/sp00nznet)) wrote [psnr](https://github.com/sp00nznet/psnr): the server, the C client, the protocol, NAT traversal, the relay and the NAT lab.

undecuple ([undecuple](https://github.com/undecuple)) maintains re-psn and wrote everything added since the fork: the release and container tooling, the AppImage, hardening and limits, rooms and invite codes, the desktop app, this website, the documentation and the tests.
